items.description: List of cksfv invocations (one per line), each with optional options and arguments. Each item defines one command-line invocation. At least one item is required (typically verification with -f, -g, or -r/-R). For multiple invocations, each item may override or add flags and paths as documented in cksfv(1). All option keys are optional; only specified ones appear in the config line for that item. No item-level defaults; omitting all options yields a no-op line (not recommended). All options correspond to documented cksfv(1) flags (see manpage). Option '-C', '-f', and '-g' accept a string path; others are boolean flags that appear when true or omitted when false/absent. Values must be absolute or relative paths as per cksfv(1) behavior. Recursion (-r/-R) should be used with care: -r verifies .sfv files in directories; -R reads checksums for all files in directories. -C and -g are mutually exclusive in practice — choose one per item. -b is primarily for creation mode but is listed here for symmetry. -L (follow symlinks) only applies with -r or -R. -i affects case sensitivity during verification. -q suppresses non-error output; -v enables verbose output (default). -c forces stdout flushing for external parsing — useful in automation scripts. Items should not repeat the same option key unnecessarily (e.g., -q then -v). Use one item for typical single-file verification: { option: '-g', value: '/path/to/file.sfv' }. Use multiple items for multi-tree verification or mixed options. Every item must be a map, not a scalar or list of strings — per schema design. All option strings MUST be one of: -b, -c, -i, -L, -q, -v, -r, -R, -C, -f, -g — no other flags exist in cksfv(1). Values for -C, -f, -g must be valid paths (strings). All items are validated at render time (Jinja2 doesn’t validate, but config tooling should). Example item: {"option": "-g", "value": "/var/checksums/files.sfv"}. For items without options, an empty object {} yields no flags (not recommended). Use only documented options. Do not add undocumented or custom options. All items must be flat; no nesting beyond the map level per item. All paths must be strings or empty; empty string for -C/-f/-g is invalid — omit the option instead. If -C or -g appear, -f is optional (but -f alone requires an explicit file). -r and -R are incompatible with -f and -g — configs must respect this (not enforced by template). Use -C for legacy -C dir -f file.sfv style, or -g file.sfv for modern path-based invocation. Prefer -g over -C in new configs. -L must be paired with -r or -R to be effective. All flags are case-sensitive (e.g., -C, not -c). All items must be scalar-serializable JSON maps (no nested objects). Items with empty string paths cause rendering errors — validate before use. Every item is independent — order matters only in execution sequence (template renders linearly). No comments in generated output beyond the template header. No indentation beyond the required single-line directives. No custom filters or extensions. All values must be string-compatible with shell escaping rules (though cksfv handles quoting internally).
